summary.whatChanges: The RPC client now only appends `?` plus the query string when the serialized search params are non-empty. Requests, `$url()`, and `$path()` no longer produce a dangling `?` when a query object yields no parameters (e.g. all-undefined values or a custom `buildSearchParams` returning nothing). Tests cover the new behavior.
behaviorChanges: Client requests with a query object that serializes to nothing now hit `/search` instead of `/search?`
`$url(...).href` and `$path(...)` omit the trailing `?` for empty serialized queries
A custom `buildSearchParams` returning an empty `URLSearchParams` no longer adds `?` to the URL
Empty-string query values are still preserved (`/search?q=`)
risks: Code or tests asserting the previous trailing-`?` URLs, or servers/proxies keying caches on that exact string, will see different URLs
Behavior only changes when the serializer yields zero params; query objects producing empty-but-present values still emit `?`
